_notes: SparkFun Qwiic Button (ATtiny84 with SparkFun firmware) at 0x6F by default (the address can be changed in software). The LED is a single colour (red or green, depending on the board), so it has brightness and pulse settings, not a colour. Every LED and debounce setting is saved in the button's EEPROM, so it survives a power cycle (a new button: brightness 255, no pulsing, debounce 10 ms). The pulse step must not be 0: the firmware divides by it. Poll: the status register (0x03), bit 2 = pressed; its clicked and event bits stay set until written back, so they aren't decoded.

rsao.note: bench (Axiom018, button on a mux slot, 2026-10-23): the lone 0x99 + 9-byte read fails with an I2C hardware timeout and the button drops off the bus for about 1.1 s, then is found and identified again; devices on other slots and the main bus are unaffected (the mux isolates the slot, the master times out after about 1.6 ms). Source: the read handler doesn't check the register pointer, so from 0x99 the length wraps to 65415 and the handler loops inside the I2C interrupt, holding the clock (Qwiic_Button e89a82f interrupts.ino 76-91). No setting changes. Its default address 0x6F is excluded from RSAO addressing

actions.desc: LED presets: off, on (full brightness, steady) or breathe (full brightness, 1 s pulse, 0.5 s off)
LED brightness, 0-255 (when pulsing, the peak of each pulse)
Brightness change at each step of a pulse, 1-255 (1 is smoothest)
Length of one pulse (ramp up and down) in ms; 0 = no pulsing, the LED stays at its brightness
Time the LED stays off between pulses, in ms
